Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 28-year-old female with 2-day constant suprapubic pain, nausea, subjective fever, urinary frequency, and recent inter-menstrual spotting. No dysuria or discharge. Contraceptive implant in situ; pregnancy status unknown.  

Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):  
• Urinary tract infection (cystitis ± early pyelonephritis) – high likelihood given suprapubic ache, urinary frequency, systemic symptoms despite absent dysuria.  
• Early intra-uterine pregnancy or ectopic pregnancy – moderate likelihood; spotting, pelvic pain, and nausea warrant exclusion despite implant use.  
• Pelvic inflammatory disease – moderate likelihood; lower-abdominal pain, spotting, systemic symptoms in sexually active woman; fewer classic features present.  
• Early/atypical appendicitis and residual constipation considered but less likely.  

Working diagnosis: Rule-out UTI vs pregnancy-related cause; other pelvic pathology to be excluded.  

Management Plan

- Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for physical examination and investigations.  
- Immediate tests to organise: urine dip and culture; serum and/or urine β-hCG to exclude pregnancy/ectopic; full set of vital signs; possible pelvic exam; FBC, CRP if indicated.  
- Safety-net advice provided: attend urgent care if pain worsens, light-headedness, syncope, increased bleeding, or other concerning symptoms develop.  
- Discussed need for further assessment to confirm or rule out UTI, PID, appendicitis, or other abdominal/pelvic pathologies.  
- No medications started during tele-consult.  

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Consider if PID suspected or for comprehensive STI screening (not yet arranged).  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded.  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Urinary tract infection (High) – suprapubic discomfort, urinary frequency, nausea/fever.  
2. Early pregnancy or ectopic pregnancy (Moderate) – pelvic pain, spotting, contraceptive failure possible.  
3. Pelvic inflammatory disease (Moderate) – pelvic pain, spotting, systemic features; needs exclusion.
